## Accession logic

GEO and SRA are linked repositories, not a single strict hierarchy. A common navigation path is:

```text
GEO metadata/processed-data layer:  GSE series -> GSM sample
                                           |
                                           | linked/brokered raw HTS data
                                           v
SRA raw-data layer:                 SRP study -> SRX experiment -> SRR run
```

The mapping is not necessarily one-to-one: a GEO sample may link to multiple SRA experiments or runs. GEO retains the metadata and processed-data layer and brokers submitted HTS raw files to SRA ([NCBI guidance](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/info/seq.html)).

The **ArrayExpress collection in BioStudies** provides functional-genomics study records and SDRF metadata. Raw HTS reads linked from the collection are brokered to ENA, which provides the run records and FASTQ download routes ([EMBL-EBI explanation](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/biostudies/arrayexpress/)). Always record which route and accessions were used.

## ArrayExpress collection in BioStudies + ENA route

The main workshop route uses the single script created in Day 1:

```text
ArrayExpress collection SDRFs from BioStudies
  -> retain the WT samples
  -> convert ENA FTP links to HTTPS
  -> add simple FASTQ filenames
  -> download the RNA-seq and ChIP-seq FASTQ files
```

The complete copy-paste code and its block-by-block explanation are in Day 1, Section 7.3. The saved script is:

```text
scripts/day1/02_download_ena_fastq.sh
```

It creates two filtered run-level metadata tables:

```text
raw_data/metadata/RNAseq_metadata.txt
raw_data/metadata/Chipseq_metadata.txt
```

Each table retains the original SDRF columns and adds `HTTPS_FASTQ_URI` and `FASTQ_NAME` as its final two columns. Separate, visible `while` loops read those final fields and download the RNA-seq and ChIP-seq files. These two tables provide the metadata used by the later workshop steps.

Run the complete retrieval directly from the project root:

```bash
bash scripts/day1/02_download_ena_fastq.sh
```

::: {.callout-note title="Optional Docker route for this download"}
If the required host commands are unavailable, the same script can run in the supplied curl image:

```bash
docker run --rm \
  --platform linux/amd64 \
  -v "$PWD:/work" \
  -w /work \
  docker.io/fgualdr/ngs-curl@sha256:5f878548820cdccec01ac62cf7db648f7a47f0541e3390cc43ab2225f072669c \
  bash scripts/day1/02_download_ena_fastq.sh
```

Containerized downloads depend on Docker's DNS, proxy, and VPN configuration. If this reports `curl: (6) Could not resolve host`, use the direct Bash command above.
:::

The reproducibility records are:

```text
raw_data/metadata/METADATA.md
results/logs/day1/metadata_fastq_download.log
```

Do not commit the downloaded FASTQ files.

## Optional GEO/SRA route

The optional Day 1 route downloads complete run-level metadata reports directly from the ENA Portal API using the two SRA study accessions:

```text
raw_data/metadata/ERP147707_metadata.tsv    RNA-seq study ERP147707
raw_data/metadata/ERP147583_metadata.tsv    ChIP-seq study ERP147583
```

No manual Run Selector download or file-moving step is required. The maintained script creates selected copies and adds the accessions and simplified paired FASTQ names needed by its download loops:

```text
scripts/day1/04_optional_sra_download.sh
  -> curl the ERP147707 and ERP147583 read_run reports
  -> keep columns 1, 73, 109, and 163 with cut
  -> rename the short table header
  -> select exact sample_title values WT_1/2/3 and WTS_1/2/3
  -> retain experiment_accession for provenance
  -> use run_accession for retrieval
  -> download each ERR run with fasterq-dump --split-files
  -> rename and compress each R1/R2 pair
```

The `ERX...` Experiment accessions are retained for provenance. The actual `fasterq-dump` argument is the associated `ERR...` Run accession because FASTQ data are retrieved at run level. This distinction matters whenever one experiment has more than one run; it also follows the [official SRA Toolkit guidance](https://github.com/ncbi/sra-tools/wiki/08.-prefetch-and-fasterq-dump).

For larger transfers, `prefetch ERR_ACCESSION` can first create a resumable local SRA copy. The workshop example deliberately uses direct `fasterq-dump ERR_ACCESSION --split-files` calls so its download loops parallel the direct `curl` route.

The API responses are TSV files requested with `fields=all`. In both reports, `run_accession` is column 1, `sample_title` is column 73, `library_layout` is column 109, and `experiment_accession` is column 163. The script verifies those headers, uses `cut` to keep only the four required fields, and adds simple column names and paired FASTQ names. It selects the six sample titles explicitly because long descriptive fields mention both genotypes on every row; a whole-line `grep -v "ΔHP1021"` would therefore remove the WT runs too.

Run the script only if the optional example is assigned:

```bash
docker run --rm \
  --platform linux/amd64 \
  -v "$PWD:/work" \
  -w /work \
  docker.io/fgualdr/ngs-sra-tools@sha256:83d9d94db767b4f13692fb576e3effc1ca0e24dab2d157273ed71bc3ec689060 \
  bash scripts/day1/04_optional_sra_download.sh
```

The selected metadata, provenance record, and log are written to:

```text
raw_data/metadata/ERP147707_metadata.tsv
raw_data/metadata/ERP147583_metadata.tsv
raw_data/metadata/ERP147707_WT_metadata.tsv
raw_data/metadata/ERP147583_WT_metadata.tsv
raw_data/metadata/SRA_METADATA.md
results/logs/day1/sra_fastq_download.log
```

The paired outputs use the same FASTQ names as the main ENA route, for example `WT_1_R1.fastq.gz` and `WT_1_R2.fastq.gz`, under `raw_data/fastq/rnaseq/` or `raw_data/fastq/chipseq/`. The SRA tables do not replace the SDRF-derived downstream design metadata used in Days 2 and 3. Use this as a future-project example unless the instructor supplies matching downstream design metadata, and do not run it over files already downloaded through ENA.

`fasterq-dump` creates large uncompressed files and requires additional scratch space. Check available disk space first, and use instructor-provided FASTQ files or checkpoints rather than starting simultaneous class-wide downloads.

The complete copy-paste script, including both `curl` commands, and its block-by-block explanation are in Day 1, Section 7.4. This remains an example route, not the main workshop download route.

## Reproducibility record

Version the accession and metadata tables. Do not version downloaded FASTQ files.
